source: VOICE Teaching Templates (draft), approved Oct 28 2026; adapted from Richard Wawrzonkowski's RBT Teaching Templates and Activity Skill Groups

clinical.cue: No spoken SD. Place {word} in view and out of reach, look at {name} expectantly, and wait 3–5 seconds. Do not ask "What do you want?"
clinical.setup: Quick preference check first. Keep VOICE within reach and never remove it as a consequence. Model {word} on the device while saying it once, without requiring imitation.
clinical.when: Snack Time, Bubbles, Pop-Up and Cause-and-Effect Toys, Car Ramp Races, Play-Doh, or any moment {name} reaches for {word}.
clinical.reinforcement: Deliver {word} immediately on selection and restate the word ("{word}!"). Brief access, then set up the next opportunity. Save the highest-value items for independent responses.
clinical.errorCorrection: A different word still speaks. Respond to it ("You want that? Let's find {word}"), model {word}, and deliver after {name} selects it. Do not deliver for the wrong word. If {name} reaches or grabs, keep the item out of reach, model, and deliver on the tap. If {name} is distressed, honor any communication attempt.
clinical.notes: Correct responses: selects {word} with or without prompts; from a new adult or room; "want" or "more" + {word}. Next step: two-word requests.

parent.cue: Hold up the {word} where {name} can see it but can't reach it. Don't ask a question; just smile and wait a few seconds.
parent.setup: Keep VOICE close to {name}. Show how it works: tap {word} yourself while saying it. Then hold the item and wait.
parent.when: Snack, play and bath time, or any time {name} wants the {word}.
parent.reinforcement: Give the {word} right away and say the word back. Getting the item is the reward: the button worked!
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} taps a different word, that's okay; answer it ("Oh, you said ball!"). Then show {word} again and give it when they tap it. If {name} is upset, give it anyway and try again later.
parent.notes: Next step: help {name} put two words together, like "want {word}" or "more {word}."

clinical.cue: No spoken SD. Start a preferred activity, then interrupt it (stop the swing, close the bubbles, hold the toy mid-action). Look expectantly and wait 3–5 seconds.
clinical.setup: Model {word} on VOICE several times during the activity before expecting it (aided language input). Plan 5–10 interruptions per activity.
clinical.when: Bubbles, Peekaboo and Tickle Games, Pop-Up Toys, Ball Ramp and Drop Tube, Song Time, Playground Time (swing, slide).
clinical.reinforcement: Resume or deliver the action immediately and narrate it ("{word}! Here we go!").
clinical.errorCorrection: Wrong word: respond to what was said, model {word}, and resume only after {word} is selected. If {name} protests with behavior, prompt {word} immediately (errorless) and resume on the tap.
clinical.notes: Expand to two words ("more bubbles," "go swing"). Probe generalization across activities and partners.

parent.cue: Start something {name} loves, then stop in the middle and wait. Look at {name} like "your turn."
parent.setup: Before stopping, tap {word} yourself a few times as you play ("{word}!"). Then pause and let {name} try.
parent.when: Swings, tickles, songs, bubbles, opening containers: anything {name} wants to keep going.
parent.reinforcement: Start the fun again right away and say the word back.
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} taps something else, answer it, then show {word} again and start the fun when they tap it. If {name} gets upset, help them tap it and start right away.
parent.notes: When {word} is easy, try two words: "more swing," "open snack."

clinical.cue: No spoken SD. For help: present a blocked task (tight lid, item out of reach, missing piece). For break, finished, stop or no: present a mildly non-preferred demand. Wait 3 seconds and prompt {word} before problem behavior begins. Follow the BCBA's FCR plan.
clinical.setup: Plan 5–10 opportunities per session. Start easy, then slightly harder. Early on, prompt immediately (errorless) and honor every request. Thin the schedule only per the BCBA plan.
clinical.when: Snack Time (sealed containers), Inset Puzzle, Getting Dressed, Cleanup Time, Arrival Routine, work tasks.
clinical.reinforcement: Deliver the help, break or end of task immediately. For break: a short timed break, then return to the task.
clinical.errorCorrection: If problem behavior occurs first, do not deliver the help or break for it. Calmly model {word} and deliver only after {name} selects it.
clinical.notes: Never remove VOICE. Treat "stop" and "no" as real communication and an assent signal: honor them, then problem-solve.

parent.cue: For "help": give {name} something they can't do alone, like a closed snack container, and wait. For "break" or "finished": start a task {name} doesn't love, and show the button before they get upset. Don't ask "Do you need help?"
parent.setup: Plan a few chances a day. At first, show the {word} button right away so {name} learns it works.
parent.when: Snacks, getting dressed, puzzles, clean-up, homework.
parent.reinforcement: Help right away, or give the break right away. That's the reward.
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} cries, throws or pushes away, stay calm, show the {word} button, and help as soon as they tap it.
parent.notes: "Stop" and "no" are real words. Listen to them, even when you can't give {name} what they want right then.

clinical.cue: Greetings: a familiar partner approaches, says "Hi, {name}!" or "Bye, {name}!" once with a wave, and waits 3–5 seconds. Turns: during a turn-taking game, pause when it's {name}'s turn. Manners: when handing an item. No "Say {word}."
clinical.setup: Plan 5–10 natural chances (staff or peers entering and leaving, game turns). The prompter stands behind {name} so prompts fade easily.
clinical.when: Arrival Routine, Circle Time, Turn-Taking Board Game, Peekaboo, end of session.
clinical.reinforcement: The partner responds warmly and keeps the interaction going (smile, high five, a quick chat).
clinical.errorCorrection: No response within 5 seconds: model {word} while the partner is still present, let {name} select it, and the partner responds warmly. Don't repeat the greeting several times.
clinical.notes: Don't require "please" or "thank you" before giving a requested item; it can become a generic request word.

parent.cue: When someone arrives or leaves, have them say "Hi, {name}!" or "Bye!" once and wait. Don't tell {name} "say hi."
parent.setup: Ask family members to greet {name} at the door and wait a moment for an answer.
parent.when: Coming home, leaving school, visitors, board games.
parent.reinforcement: Answer happily and keep playing or talking with {name}.
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} doesn't answer, tap {word} for them while the person is still there, and let {name} try. Don't keep repeating "hi."
parent.notes: It's fine to give {name} what they asked for even without "please."

clinical.cue: Hold up or point to {word} (object or picture), gain attention, and ask "What is it?" once. Wait 3–5 seconds.
clinical.setup: One target item at a time; mix in a mastered label every 2–3 trials. Move from pictures to real items to the natural environment.
clinical.when: Farm Animal Barn, Shared Storybook, Mystery Bag, Show and Tell, walks, Circle Time.
clinical.reinforcement: Praise and social interaction (or token). Do not hand over the item, which turns the label into a request.
clinical.errorCorrection: Incorrect or no response: "Listen, it's a {word}," model on VOICE, wait for {name} to select it, then repeat the trial once and reinforce.
clinical.notes: Probe across exemplars (different pictures, colors, sizes of {word}).

parent.cue: Point to the {word} (in a book, on a walk, a toy) and ask once, "What is it?" Then wait.
parent.setup: Look at books and real things together. Ask about {word} now and then, mixed with words {name} already knows.
parent.when: Books, walks, the zoo, toy animals, pictures on the phone.
parent.reinforcement: Cheer and talk about it ("Yes, a {word}! It says moo!").
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} picks another word, say "It's a {word}," tap it, and let them try again.
parent.notes: Use different examples: big and small, real and pictures.

clinical.cue: No spoken SD. Create something interesting (a surprise, a new toy, an unexpected event), then pause and look at {name} expectantly for 3–5 seconds. Don't ask a question.
clinical.setup: Model 2–3 comments on VOICE first ("Wow!" "Look!"), then reduce your own comments over the session.
clinical.when: Pop-Up Toys, Magna-Tile Tower, Car Ramp Races, Sensory Bin, Joke Book Time, Show and Tell.
clinical.reinforcement: Respond with excitement to any comment and expand it by 1–2 words ("Wow! Big tower!").
clinical.errorCorrection: No comment: model {word}, wait for {name} to select it, respond enthusiastically. Don't treat a request ("more") as a comment; honor the request, then model the comment.
clinical.notes: Comments are shared enjoyment, not a request; nothing is delivered.

parent.cue: Make something fun or surprising happen (a tower falls, a toy pops up), then pause and look at {name}. Don't ask anything.
parent.setup: Tap {word} yourself a few times when fun things happen, then give {name} a turn.
parent.when: Knocking down towers, funny faces, bubbles popping, silly books.
parent.reinforcement: React with excitement and add a word: "Wow, so tall!"
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} stays quiet, tap {word} for them, wait, and celebrate when they copy it.
parent.notes: There's no prize here; the fun of sharing is the reward.

clinical.cue: Two contexts. Labeling: show one clear face or picture and ask "How does he feel?" once; wait 5 seconds. In the moment: when {name} shows the feeling or need, pause and model {word} on VOICE.
clinical.setup: Start with 2 contrasting feelings (happy, sad), then add more. Move from cartoons to photos to real people. For body parts, pair with "my" and "hurt" ("my tummy hurt").
clinical.when: Feelings Charades, Shared Storybook, Bath and Lotion Time (body parts), Calm down routines, any real moment of the feeling.
clinical.reinforcement: In the moment: respond to the message functionally ("You're tired. Let's rest."). Labeling: praise.
clinical.errorCorrection: Labeling: show the same card, model {word}, have {name} select it, then present a mastered card. In the moment: model only; don't quiz a child who is upset.
clinical.notes: Always take reports of hurt, sick or pain seriously and check, even during teaching.

parent.cue: When {name} looks tired, happy or upset, say what you see and tap {word} ("You look {word}"). You can also look at faces in books and ask "How does he feel?"
parent.setup: Start with happy and sad. Use real moments as often as you can.
parent.when: When {name} is happy, upset, tired or hurt; bath time for body parts; books.
parent.reinforcement: Answer what {name} told you: "You're hungry? Let's get a snack."
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} picks a different feeling, gently show {word}. If {name} is upset, just show the word and comfort them; don't quiz.
parent.notes: Always check when {name} says "hurt" or "sick," even if you're practicing.

clinical.cue: Yes/no: offer a clearly preferred or clearly non-preferred item ("Do you want ___?"), wait 3–5 seconds. Question words: contrive an information gap (hide a favorite item for "where," a new person for "who," a mystery bag for "what") and pause.
clinical.setup: Yes/no: alternate preferred and non-preferred items so both answers are reinforced. Question words: model the question on VOICE yourself during play first.
clinical.when: Snack Time choices, Mystery Bag, Dollhouse, hide-and-find games, Weather and Calendar Routine.
clinical.reinforcement: Honor the answer exactly: "yes" gets the item, "no" removes it. For questions, answer and give access to what was hidden.
clinical.errorCorrection: If the answer doesn't match behavior (says yes, pushes away), model the matching word and honor it. Don't test "no" with items the learner actually wants.
clinical.notes: Honoring "no" is an assent practice; respect it in all sessions.

parent.cue: For yes and no: hold up something {name} loves or dislikes and ask "Do you want it?" For question words: hide a favorite toy and wait for "where."
parent.setup: Mix things {name} wants and doesn't want, so both "yes" and "no" get practice.
parent.when: Snack choices, hide-and-seek with toys, "what's in the bag?"
parent.reinforcement: Do what {name} said: give it for "yes," take it away for "no." Answer their questions and show them.
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} says "yes" but pushes it away, show "no" and take it away.
parent.notes: When {name} says "no," listen whenever you can.

clinical.cue: Present 2–3 preferred items that differ only on the target concept (a red and a blue car). Ask "Which one?" once or wait expectantly; the learner selects {word} to get that item.
clinical.setup: One concept dimension per block (color, size, or number). Rotate positions. Mix in mastered concepts between new trials.
clinical.when: Car Ramp Races, Magna-Tile Tower, Counting-Bear Snack, Coloring and Drawing, Play-Doh, Mr. Potato Head.
clinical.reinforcement: Deliver the chosen item (the {word} one) immediately and restate ("The {word} one!").
clinical.errorCorrection: If {name} selects the item word without the concept, model {word} + item and deliver after the concept word. If the wrong concept is selected, deliver that item (honor it) and model {word} on the next trial.
clinical.notes: Combine with the item for two-word requests ("big cookie," "red car").

parent.cue: Hold up two of the same thing that differ in one way (a big and a little cookie). Ask "Which one?" and wait.
parent.setup: Practice one kind of word at a time, like colors one day and sizes another.
parent.when: Snack (big or little piece), crayons, cars, building blocks.
parent.reinforcement: Give {name} the one they picked and say the word back.
parent.errorCorrection: If {name} picks the other color or size, give them that one (they asked for it!), then show {word} next time.
parent.notes: Next step: two words together, like "{word} car."

clinical.cue: No specific SD. Model {word} on VOICE frequently during natural conversation and activities, and create chances where {word} is useful.
clinical.setup: Use aided language input: say and tap {word} together during real interactions, several times per activity.
clinical.when: Any routine or play where {word} naturally fits.
clinical.reinforcement: Respond to the message {name} sent and keep the interaction going.
clinical.errorCorrection: Respond to whatever {name} said, then model {word} in a short phrase.

parent.cue: Use {word} yourself on VOICE often while you talk and play.
parent.setup: Say and tap {word} together during everyday moments.
parent.when: Any time {word} fits what you're doing.
parent.reinforcement: Answer what {name} said and keep talking or playing.
parent.errorCorrection: Answer whatever {name} said, then show {word} in a short phrase.

assignment.description: Starting template per word; adult can switch any target to another template.

social: Chat page and its folders (greetings, turns, manners)
commenting: Chat comments (wow, uh oh, cool, yuck, I like it, that's funny)

assignment.note: Word-level assignments (byWordId) take priority over page assignments. Match by the app's real word ids; 'no' appears in both help-break and yes-no-questions: use help-break.
